markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback favors specific recent connections over broad similarity. This motivates testing recent-context dependence, without treating feedback as proof that older interactions are irrelevant. (2) Existing margins depend on logit scale and sampled negatives. Matched target ranks provide a complementary diagnostic. (3) Compatibility and replacement needs are often unknown. Titles and descriptions can support tentative annotations, but cannot establish ownership or practical fit.

**Related work.** (1) NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions impose a receptive field [1]. Context probes must respect reachable positions and verify causal behavior. (2) Sampled ranking can reverse model comparisons [2]. Training-prefix diagnostics and full-catalog feedback must remain separate from pinned validation HR@10. (3) Repeated validation selection introduces selection bias [3]. A small, predefined ablation is preferable at this initial research stage.

These insights suggest three directions: causal context auditing, adaptive recent-context representation, and evidence-grounded feedback annotation.

## Framework

| Direction | Observable evidence | Intervention | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context dependence | Paired prefix target ranks | Recent/old deletion and shuffling | Dependence does not establish intent |
| Adaptive context | Recent versus full-context features | One jointly trained residual gate | Accuracy improvement requires validation |
| Feedback grounding | Exact title/description spans | Supported/contradicted/unknown labels | Similarity cannot prove compatibility |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality / future potential / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Matched context audit: 4/7/3.** Freeze NextItNet and compare equal-count recent and old deletions with fixed candidates [1,2]. Positive: inexpensive, interpretable model-dependence evidence. Negative: perturbations can create unrealistic histories; the contribution is primarily methodological.
2. **Recent-context residual gate: 5/7/4 — selected.** Add one jointly trained gate between full-history and recent-history NextItNet representations, sharing every backbone parameter [1]. Positive: a small intervention directly tests adaptive recency. Negative: extra computation and a risk of discarding useful long-range evidence.
3. **Evidence-grounded feedback audit: 4/6/4.** Annotate recommendation–history relationships using supporting text spans and explicit unknowns [4]. Positive: exposes unsupported compatibility claims. Negative: annotation quality and twenty-user coverage limit conclusions; it does not directly optimize ranking.

## Selected algorithm

For each category, train one NextItNet with a shared backbone evaluated on the full history and its last eight interactions. Compute `g = sigmoid(MLP([h_full, h_recent]))`, then `h = LayerNorm(h_full + g * (h_recent - h_full))`. Score items through the existing item embedding and preserve the baseline loss. This is one jointly trained network and checkpoint; there are no separately fitted predictors.

Use correct left-padding readout, causal convolutions, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the fixed 200-epoch/200-batch limits. Preserve routing, `GAGC_DATA_DIR`, ModelView interfaces, diagnostic entry points, and identical predictor reconstruction. Compare baseline against this single predefined variant using macro validation HR@10; claim no improvement before measurement.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163; [2] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [3] https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html; [4] https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08839.

idea.description: Add an adaptive recent-context residual gate to one NextItNet model per category. The same causal convolutional backbone processes full and recent histories; a jointly trained gate interpolates their representations before the existing item scorer.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests that broad historical relevance sometimes displaces specific recent interests. A shared-backbone gate tests whether adaptive recent-context emphasis improves pinned validation HR@10 while retaining access to longer context. This is a hypothesis, not an established diagnosis or measured improvement.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from the supplied corrected NextItNet baseline. Fix the recent window to eight interactions for this initial experiment; preserve chronological order and left padding. Share all backbone and item-embedding parameters across both passes. Mix per-position features so log2feats returns B×L×D and predict_score remains compatible; construct each recent window only from that position's causal prefix. Use the final nonpadding index for sequence readout, never count−1. Preserve sample_batch, ModelView, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return unavailable diagnostics as null with sample counts and definitions. Preserve the baseline objective, splits, negative sampling, four-category routing, seeds, maximum epochs 200, and batches per epoch 200. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save one checkpoint per category under the trial directory. Embed the exact shared-backbone gate architecture and configuration in the predictor writer. Do not add independent scores or reuse other trials. The extra backbone pass increases compute, so assess runtime within the shared budget.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category independently:
  initialize one NextItNet backbone F, item embeddings E, and gate G
  for each baseline training batch:
    H_full = F(left_padded_sequence)
    for each supervised position t:
      W_t = left_pad(last_8_nonpadding_items(sequence[:t+1]))
    H_recent = final_nonpadding_features(F(batched_W_t))
    gate = sigmoid(G(concat(H_full, H_recent)))
    H = LayerNorm(H_full + gate * (H_recent - H_full))
    optimize baseline_loss(predict_score(H, positives), predict_score(H, negatives))
  save one joint checkpoint and matching predictor configuration
Compare the predefined baseline and variant using the pinned macro validation HR@10. Use matched training-prefix context perturbations only as explanatory diagnostics.

originality.positive: Combines adaptive recency with a parameter-shared causal convolutional recommender through a small, testable intervention.
originality.negative: Gated short- and long-context representations are established techniques; novelty is primarily in the constrained application and evaluation.

future_potential.positive: Could support subsequent research into when recent context helps, using measured context dependence and history-length strata.
future_potential.negative: A gate cannot infer compatibility, replacement needs, or user intent from interaction sequences alone.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing backbone, scorer, objective, and checkpoint structure with a small added module.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient causal windows at every training position and exact agreement between training, ModelView, and embedded inference require careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal dilated convolutions and residual blocks for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone preserved by the proposed shared-parameter context gate.
limitations: A finite receptive field constrains which historical interactions can affect a prediction.
Sequence dependence alone does not establish current purpose or compatibility.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can produce inconsistent model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not make training-prefix diagnostics interchangeable with the task's pinned validation benchmark.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated optimization of a model-selection criterion can bias reported performance.
limitations: Does not provide a task-specific estimate of selection bias for these four datasets.

related_work.title: Inferring Networks of Substitutable and Complementary Products
contributions: Distinguishes substitute and complement product relationships, motivating more precise feedback annotation.
limitations: Product relationships do not establish user ownership, replacement intent, or instance-specific compatibility.
Its data assumptions must not be imported into this task, where reviews and several metadata fields are unavailable.
